result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. I didn't add a test or run the new patterns against example paths, and the `*Scoping*` test run printed nothing and showed no failures.

The change is in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, lines 410–411. The two regexes went from `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `(.*/)?mock[^/]*/.*`, and the `__mock` one the same way. The `[^/]*` keeps the match inside a single folder name. Because the match starts at a folder boundary, `remock/` and `demo/` don't match, and neither do files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`.

I didn't touch backslash handling. Paths are already normalised to `/` before the conventions are applied, so Windows-style paths go through the same regexes.

The old folder shapes (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) all still fit the new patterns.

The leading `(.*/)?` also lets a `mock` folder at the very start of a relative path match, which the old patterns didn't allow.
